Questa ottimizzazione accelera gli accessi alla memoria da parte del programma guest. Abilitandola, le letture/scritture della memoria guest vengono eseguite direttamente in memoria e sfruttano la MMU host. Disabilitandola, tutti gli accessi alla memoria sono costretti a utilizzare l\'emulazione software della MMU.

STORM SWITCH is a performance-focused fork of the Eden emulator. It integrates dedicated ARM64 NCE optimizations, custom GPU driver management (Turnip/Mesa), full GameBanana mod support, TitleDB metadata integration, and 10 exclusive STORM themes.

• Eden Project & Team — original project & core emulator foundation
• Yuzu & Citra Teams — groundbreaking emulation codebase
• Ryujinx Team — invaluable reverse engineering & Switch HLE research
• Skyline / Strato Team — ARM64 NCE and Android performance techniques
• Mesa, Freedreno & Turnip Teams — open-source Vulkan driver development
• Global open-source emulation contributors
People who make STORM SWITCH and Eden possible
When Turbo Mode is enabled, emulation will run at this speed.
When Slow Mode is enabled, emulation will run at this speed.
Command-line arguments passed to homebrew at launch (e.g. -noglsl).
Raises the clock the emulated CPU reports, which removes some FPS limiters. Weaker CPUs may see reduced performance, and certain games may behave improperly.
Determines how sharpened the image will look while using FSR or SGSR filters
Controls the GPU emulation mode. Most games render fine with Fast, but Accurate is still required for some. Particles tend to only render correctly with Accurate mode.

Controls the GPU fence synchronization behavior. Immediate is the fastest option, but can introduce some issues. Balanced offers better compatibility and may fix issues in some games. Accurate further improves compatibility at the cost of some performance. Strict is the slowest option, but can fix issues that require stricter synchronization. Default follows the GPU Accuracy setting.
Recompresses ASTC textures to BC1, BC3, or BC5 formats on the fly to reduce RAM and VRAM usage by 50–80%.
This hack can increase performance by running GPU emulation asynchronously at the cost of graphical issues and increased crash rates by timing-related operations.
This hack can increase performance by moving presentation to a separate CPU thread at the cost of graphical issues.
Enables access to previous buffer states. This option may improve rendering quality and performance consistency in some games.

Preserves GPU-modified buffer data by reading it back before uploads. Some games require this to render certain effects properly. May cause issues if the hardware cannot handle the additional workload.
Enables optimized vertex buffer binding for improved performance. Requires Mesa 26.0+ Turnip drivers/ QCOM drivers. Will crash on older Turnip drivers (25.3 and below).
Prevents 0 FPS deadlocks in games like Ori 2, DKCR:HD, Subnautica Below Zero by minimizing frame wait latency.
Passes shaders through spirv-opt to reduce driver compile overhead, eliminate stutter, and keep SoC cooler.
Skips intermediate non-critical frames during rendering dips, maintaining smooth gameplay speed and lower temperatures.
Smooths out frame transitions by interpolating consecutive frames.
Makes the game believe GPU work finishes faster than it does, so it stops lowering resolution and render distance to fit the Switch\'s clocks.
Reduces bloom blur in LA/EOW (Adreno A6XX - A7XX/ Turnip), removes bloom in Burnout. Warning: may cause graphical artifacts in other games.
Fixes problems with inverted colors in games or strange artifacts or strange shadows.
Enables a legacy handling for the rescale configuration pass for games by using a quick rescale path
Configure GPU-based texture unswizzling parameters or disable it entirely. Adjust these settings to balance performance and texture loading quality.

Sets the maximum size (MB) for GPU-based texture unswizzling. While the GPU is faster for medium and large textures, the CPU may be more efficient for very small ones. Adjust this to find the balance between GPU acceleration and CPU overhead.

Sets the data limit per frame for unswizzling large textures. Higher values speed up texture loading at the cost of higher frame latency; lower values reduce GPU overhead but may cause visible texture pop-in.
Defines the number of depth slices processed per batch for 3D textures. Increasing this improves throughput efficiency on powerful GPUs but may cause stuttering or driver timeouts on weaker hardware.

Controls the number of features that can be used in ExtendedDynamicState (EDS). The higher value will allow to reduce the amount of pipeline compilations based on the dynamic state supported by driver.
Enabling this feature allows for more flexible vertex input handling, potentially reducing pipeline compilation time in vertex/buffer.
Allows the fragment shader to execute per sample in a multi-sampled fragment instead once per fragment. Improves graphics quality at the cost of some performance.
